summary: Full daily Power Stack investment refresh. One new uranium development-stage candidate cleared the quality bar: NexGen Energy (NXE) at 8.3 after final construction approval, construction commencement and reported strategic financing discussions with BHP. No other new ticker was promoted. Power/Grid remains the core category; Water/Cooling remains the strongest new diversification sleeve; Agriculture stays selective; Healthcare/Metabolic remains concentrated in LLY and DXCM; Robotics adoption order is unchanged. July remains the latest official ISM dataset, so the ISM snapshot was re-verified but not rewritten for timestamp-only churn.

macro.rates: Long-duration valuation pressure increased as the U.S. 30-year Treasury yield reached its highest level since 2007 amid fiscal/debt-supply concerns.
macro.fx: The dollar weakened after softer U.S. economic data reduced expectations for an immediate Fed hike.
macro.oil: Brent moved back above $90 as Middle East/Hormuz risk increased. This reinforces oil/refining as a tactical hedge but also raises inflation and discount-rate risk for long-duration equities.
macro.equities: U.S. equities moved modestly off record highs as higher oil and long-end yields outweighed still-strong earnings growth.
macro.metals: Copper remains structurally supported by electrification and data-centre demand; BHP reported copper operational earnings exceeding iron ore, reinforcing the long-run copper-capex thesis without requiring another miner promotion today.

categoryRead.Power / Grid: Still the highest-conviction category. Gas-turbine orders, T&D equipment demand, switchgear/substation constraints and data-centre power requirements remain stronger evidence than broad AI-beta. Keep preference for GEV, ETN, PWR, HUBB and POWL over indiscriminate merchant-generator exposure.
categoryRead.AI / Data centres: Positive but valuation-sensitive. Rising long-end yields and debt-funded AI capex increase the need to own bottlenecks with visible orders/backlogs rather than generic AI beneficiaries.
categoryRead.Water / Cooling: Remains the strongest new diversification sleeve. ECL, MOD and XYL still clear the bar: ECL combines industrial/ultrapure water with CoolIT direct liquid cooling; MOD offers higher-beta hyperscale thermal management; XYL offers broad water infrastructure/reuse with low AI dependency.
categoryRead.Nuclear: No core-ranking change. BWXT and operating nuclear/utilities remain preferred for current earnings quality.
categoryRead.Uranium / Fuel: Strengthened. NXE is promoted to 8.3 as the preferred higher-beta development-stage satellite after construction approval/start and reported BHP financing discussions. CCJ remains the core producer/services exposure and LEU the strategic U.S. enrichment scarcity play.
categoryRead.Oil & Gas: Tactical-positive as a geopolitical hedge, but higher oil also tightens financial conditions. Prefer quality integrated producers, gas infrastructure and selective refiners over marginal upstream beta.
categoryRead.Metals: Copper remains structurally attractive. BHP's latest results show copper surpassing iron ore as its largest operational earnings contributor, validating the demand thesis without changing the current Power Stack ticker set.
categoryRead.Robotics / Automation: No hierarchy change: warehouse/fixed automation first, then cobots/mobile manipulation, industrial humanoids, and only later general-purpose consumer robots. No new evidence today justifies leapfrogging SYM/Geekplus/CGNX/TER with a humanoid OEM.
categoryRead.Agriculture / Food Systems: Still selective. CTVA remains the preferred agriculture productivity/IP exposure. VMI remains useful as irrigation plus grid infrastructure, but current irrigation volumes are still soft, so no conviction upgrade.
categoryRead.Healthcare / Metabolic: LLY and DXCM remain the preferred paired exposures: therapeutics plus monitoring. Lilly's retatrutide pipeline strengthens long-term franchise depth, but valuation and obesity-franchise concentration still cap conviction.

ism.status: Re-verified; no newer official report exists as of this run.
ism.powerStackRead: Still supportive of physical bottlenecks: manufacturing orders/production/backlog remain strong, customer inventories remain too low, and electrical/electronic components, integrated circuits, memory, semiconductors, copper and related inputs remain in short supply. Services demand is resilient but employment contracted and prices accelerated, which is consistent with a slower-growth/high-cost backdrop rather than an uncomplicated boom.

promotions.reason: Rook I has final federal construction approval, site construction has begun, and reported BHP discussions introduce credible strategic-capital optionality. Financing is not complete, so NXE remains a satellite rather than replacing CCJ as the core uranium exposure.

notPromoted: No additional Water/Cooling, Agriculture, Healthcare or Robotics name improved diversification or risk-adjusted quality enough to justify promotion today.
BHP strengthened the copper thesis but remains too diversified to displace cleaner existing Power Stack exposures solely on the basis of copper strength.

liveDesk.read: Live Desk context was available but the AI/Data Centres theme was marked stale/neutral, so it did not mechanically alter conviction scores.

researchGaps: Need a reliable live valuation feed for consistent forward P/E, EV/EBITDA and FCF-yield comparisons across every Power Stack name.
Malaysia-listed water-treatment and data-centre cooling exposure remains underdeveloped relative to the U.S. sleeve.
NXE financing terms need to be monitored: strategic discussions are not equivalent to funded construction until capital structure and dilution are known.
